post.caption: Faberge hid a train in an egg. In 1900, Tsar Nicholas the Second gave his wife a Faberge Easter egg celebrating the railway across Siberia, then nearly finished. The silver egg has green enamel and stands 26 centimeters tall, and an engraved band maps the line with the unfinished stretch dotted. Inside is a clockwork model train in gold and platinum, with signs for ladies only and smoking and a tiny chapel for its last car. Gems are the engine's lamps, and a gold key winds it. It has been kept in Moscow's Kremlin Armoury since 1927.
